//: The core's .claude/settings.json (layer 5). Two hard paths (Spec §12): the hooks (deterministic guardrails before/after an action) and permissions.deny (a blocklist evaluated by the permission engine itself). Structure per the Claude Code documentation. Hooks are invoked through bash explicitly: under Windows/PowerShell, a .sh called directly runs NOTHING, without an error, and the guard would fail open in silence (real install, 2026-08-06). This file and .claude/hooks/ change through upgrade.sh or by the user's hand, never through the agent's file tools (guard.sh rule 4), except in a session where the user said "admin GO" (admin-go.sh, on UserPromptSubmit): then they are open for that session, every write traced.

permissions.//: Second hard path (Spec §12): a blocklist evaluated before any call, redundant with guard.sh by design (defense in depth), not a replacement. An Edit(...) rule covers every file-editing tool (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit); Claude Code ignores Write(...) rules with a warning, so none is written. The guardrail's own files are NOT listed here since 0.13: a deny rule outranks every hook, and Claude Code applies Edit(...) rules to shell redirections too, so a deny would keep them shut even after the user's admin GO (observed 2026-10-05). guard.sh rule 4 holds them instead, for the file tools and the shell, and a hook deny holds in every permission mode, bypass included.
